**Tier 5** — results — pinned to dataset + policy + engine version · owned by `engine` · `public.simulation_cache`

**One row is** One cached payload of the RETIRED batch pipeline, per project and cache key: baseline data, scenario data, network analysis or risk factors that the legacy `simulation-cache-manager` stored with a time-to-live so the next legacy run could skip recomputing it. Tier 5 — derived, disposable, input to nothing that still runs. DORMANT IN THE REPOSITORY: no code in `src/`, `supabase/functions/`, `sim-worker/` or `scsim/` reads or writes it. The current product's cache is a different mechanism entirely — `analysis_get_or_start` keyed on the graph hash, and the run reuse that `simulation_runs` performs.

A RETIRED PIPELINE'S CACHE, LEFT IN PLACE ON PURPOSE by the 2026-07-02 commit that removed the legacy batch stack. A drop needs a production row count first, which no §15 run has taken. A cache whose writer is gone holds nothing anyone should trust: `data_hash` is a hash of the PAYLOAD, not of the inputs that produced it, so a hit could never say whether the project had changed since — which is the defect the graph-hash-keyed analysis store exists to avoid (`input-hash`, I5).

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | **no user-facing write path** |
| Minimum project role | `viewer` |
| Tier transitions audited | **no** — invariant `audit-actor` is not met here yet |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 2 — all carry a predicate |

Two policies through the project's organization (`org_is_current_user_org(p.organization_id, p.organization)`): SELECT for any member of that organization, ALL for the project's modeler or an organization admin. Neither is predicate-less, so `write: null` agrees with `governanceEnforcement.test.ts`, and no user-facing write path exists in the repository. `cleanup_simulation_cache()` (SECURITY DEFINER, deletes expired rows) still exists and has no caller; nothing schedules it, so expired rows are not removed — `expires_at` is a statement of intent, not a guarantee. Deleting a project removes its rows through the inline `REFERENCES projects ON DELETE CASCADE`. NOT IN PRODUCTION'S CASE: §4 D168 found `simulation-cache-manager` and `simulation-availability-checker`, the legacy functions that wrote and read this table, still LIVE in production with no source here. NOT AUDITED: tier 5, and `audit-actor` covers tiers 2–4.

## Columns

`CSV header` is the name the **user types**, which is not always the column name —
that gap is defect D21. A dash means the column has no CSV origin.

| Column | CSV header | Type | Unit | Required in CSV | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` 🔑 | — | `uuid` | — | — | Surrogate key. The row's identity is (project_id, cache_key). |
| `project_id` | — | `uuid` | — | — | The owning project; half of the unique key. `REFERENCES projects ON DELETE CASCADE`, inline. |
| `cache_key` | — | `text` | — | — | The legacy caller's name for the cached thing, unique within a project. Its composition was the caller's convention and is not recoverable from the schema. |
| `cache_type` | — | `text` | — | — | What kind of payload `data` is: 'baseline_data' (DEFAULT), 'scenario_data', 'network_analysis' or 'risk_factors' (CHECK `simulation_cache_cache_type_check`). |
| `data` | — | `jsonb` | — | — | The cached payload itself, shaped by whichever legacy computation produced it. NOT NULL. |
| `data_hash` | — | `text` | — | — | A hash of `data` as stored, computed by the writer. It identifies the payload, NOT the inputs the payload was computed from, so it cannot tell a reader whether the cache is stale. |
| `created_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When the row was inserted. |
| `expires_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When the entry stops being valid — DEFAULT 24 hours after insert; the legacy manager set it from a per-call TTL and read only unexpired rows. |
| `access_count` | — | `integer` | — | — | How many times the legacy manager served this entry; it incremented the count on every hit. |
| `last_accessed_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When the entry was last served. The defaults trigger also re-stamps it on every insert and update, so it is a write time as much as a read time. |
| `data_version` | — | `integer` | — | — | A version number for the payload format, DEFAULT 1; the legacy manager always wrote 1. |
| `dependencies` | — | `text[]` | — | — | Names of what the entry depended on, for invalidation by the caller. Free text, DEFAULT empty; nothing ever invalidated by it in the schema. |
| `organization` | — | `text` | — | — | The organization's NAME at write time, DEFAULT 'default_org'. Legacy tenancy text; the policies read the project's organization instead. |
